title: Expansion of PM Jan Aushadhi Kendras in West Bengal and coverage of uncovered blocks
body_text:
The Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the implementing agency of Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushdhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has not received any proposal from the Government of West Bengal for expansion of 469 new Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) in the State.
As on 30.06.2026, a total of 1,014 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened in the State of West Bengal, out of which, 715 JAKs have been opened across the 217 blocks of State. The district-wise number of JAKs opened in West Bengal is at Annexure-I . Block-wise number of JAKs is at Annexure-II . Out of total 345 blocks of the State, 128 blocks do not have any Jan Aushadhi Kendra, List of the same is at Annexure-III.

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers stated that the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) has not received any proposal from the West Bengal government for opening 469 new Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (JAKs). As of 30 June 2026, West Bengal had 1,014 JAKs, of which 715 are spread across 217 of the state's 345 development blocks, leaving 128 blocks without any Jan Aushadhi Kendra. District- and block-wise data were provided, showing concentration in urban/peri-urban districts like North 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Hooghly and Howrah, and gaps mainly in blocks of Murshidabad, Purulia, Birbhum and Malda.
enrichment.context:
The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), launched in 2008 and implemented by PMBI under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, aims to make quality generic medicines available at affordable prices through dedicated Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country, thereby reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure, especially for the poor and in underserved areas. The scheme has expanded rapidly in recent years, with the government targeting a much larger network of JAKs to improve last-mile access to essential medicines, particularly in rural and semi-urban blocks that currently lack such outlets.

This reply highlights a governance gap: expansion of JAKs in a state depends partly on proposals or facilitation from state governments (for premises, licenses, etc.), and the absence of a proposal from West Bengal for 469 additional kendras signals stalled coordination between the Centre and the state on this front. The uneven district- and block-level distribution—heavy clustering in Kolkata's metropolitan belt versus large swathes of blocks in Murshidabad, Purulia and Malda with zero coverage—reflects a broader pattern seen in many health access schemes, where urban and economically better-off areas benefit disproportionately, raising questions about equitable last-mile delivery of affordable healthcare.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is implemented through which of the following agencies?
options: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI)
prelims_questions.explanation: As stated in the release, PMBI is the implementing agency of PMBJP under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

prelims_questions.question: Which Ministry administers the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
prelims_questions.explanation: The release identifies the Department of Pharmaceuticals under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers as the parent ministry overseeing PMBJP through PMBI.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) and examine the challenges in ensuring equitable distribution of Jan Aushadhi Kendras across rural and urban blocks, with reference to recent data from West Bengal.

Access to affordable generic medicines is central to achieving universal health coverage in India. Critically evaluate the role of Centre-State coordination in the successful implementation of health-related welfare schemes.
